question: Who took the missing manuscript from the locked archive?

sentences_template.text: Late on a Tuesday evening, an unpublished manuscript worth a small fortune disappeared from the locked archive room at Thornwood Press.
Three editors were still in the building that night, each holding a key to the archive and each closely involved with the manuscript: {SUSPECTS}.

{TRAP} had spent the previous week loudly insisting that the manuscript should have been assigned to them, and a junior designer recalled seeing {TRAP} walking down the archive corridor that very evening.
When the theft came up the next morning, {TRAP} grew defensive and abruptly changed the subject.
The archive door's electronic log shows it was opened at 9:10 p.m. with a valid staff key, and security found no broken locks or signs of forced entry anywhere in the building.
{TRAP}'s building badge recorded them leaving through the lobby at 8:50 p.m., and the lobby camera shows {TRAP} walking out the front doors a full twenty minutes before the archive was opened.
{THIRD} spent the evening in the glass-walled conference room on a video call with an overseas author; the call's recording runs unbroken from 8:00 to 9:30 p.m.
The manuscript had been the subject of a fierce bidding war, and several outside publishers had been desperate to acquire it.
All three editors denied having taken the manuscript.
